## Part A Arithmetic Operations
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5

a + b
a - b
a * b
a / b

a%%b
a%/%b

2^10
```

Question #1: 
The 17 / 5 gives the exact floating point quotient. While 17 %/% 5 gives the integer quotient, like how many 5 fits into 17 which is 3. The 17 %% 5 on the other hand, gives the remainder which is 2.

Questions #2:
I was correct 

## Part B Basic Data Types

```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L        
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i

typeof(x)
typeof(y)
typeof(z)
typeof(w)
typeof(v)

class(x)
class(y)
class(z)
class(w)
class(v)

mode(x)
mode(y)
mode(z)
mode(w)
mode(v)

```

Question #1: 
It holds the same mathematical value but its different because the 42 is stored as a decimal number. While 42L is stored as a whole number.

## Part C Type Conversion

```{r}
num_string <- "123"
num_val <- as.numeric(num_string)

typeof(num_val)
class(num_val)
mode(num_val) 

as.logical(0) 
as.logical(1) 

as.numeric(bad_string)
```

Question #1:
So that the code won't crash, instead it gives a warning because R is built for large datasets

The risks is that you will have missing data and non accurate calculations

Question #2:
The as.logical(2) and as.logical(-1) will produce 2 TRUE

I learned that if I type 0, it produces FALSE and any none zero automatically produces TRUE

## Part D Strings, paste(), and paste0()

```{r}
first_name <- "Jonas"
last_name <- "Guardapavo"

print(first_name)
print(last_name)
cat(first_name, last_name, "\n")

full_name_paste  <- paste(first_name, last_name)
full_name_paste0 <- paste0(first_name, last_name)

print(full_name_paste)
print(full_name_paste0)

paste(first_name, last_name, sep = "-")

full_name <- paste(first_name, last_name)
paste0(full_name, " is ", age, " years old.")

```
